songs.name: And We Bid You Good Night

ai_show_review.summary: Epic Dark Star suite with tight St. Stephen > Mason's flow
ai_show_review.blurb: The Fox Theatre show is anchored by a soaring Dark Star that stretches into a seamless Saint Stephen → Mason’s Children transition. Pigpen’s soulful Lovelight and the high‑energy Good Lovin' / Uncle John’s segment add dynamic contrast, all captured on excellent soundboard tapes.
ai_show_review.review: February 2, 1970 at St. Louis’ Fox Theatre captures a Grateful Dead in peak early‑70 form. The highlight is an epic Dark Star that showcases Garcia’s “beautiful and fiery” solo work, flowing effortlessly into Saint Stephen and then the punchy Mason’s Children—a sequence reviewers call “flawless.” Pigpen’s harmonica on Turn On Your Lovelight adds a soulful touch, while the band rides a high‑energy wave through Good Lovin' into Uncle John’s Band. The rhythm section is locked in: Phil’s bass underpins the improvisations, Bob lays down solid grooves, and Mickey and Billy drive the drums with power (even if Mickey gets ahead of the beat on “Hard To Handle”). The Miller‑Gans and Vernon soundboards deliver crystal‑clear mixes that let every nuance shine, making this one of the standout early‑1970 performances.

best_recording.reason: Excellent soundboard with crystal‑clear mix, full set capture and only a tiny cut in Mason’s Children; preserves the epic Dark Star suite and all key transitions.

key_highlights: Epic Dark Star with soaring Garcia solo work
Flawless Saint Stephen → Mason’s Children transition
Pigpen’s soulful contribution on Turn On Your Lovelight
High‑energy Good Lovin' / Uncle John's Band finish

band_performance.Jerry: Garcia delivers a beautiful, fiery solo on Dark Star and soars throughout the set, especially in the St. Stephen → Mason’s Children stretch.
band_performance.Phil: Lesh provides a solid, supportive bass foundation that locks into the improvisational flow of the long jams.
band_performance.Bob: Weir adds steady rhythm and tasteful fills, contributing to the groove on Good Lovin' and Uncle John's Band.
band_performance.Mickey: Hart’s drumming is strong overall, though he gets a bit ahead of the beat on Hard To Handle; still drives the high‑energy sections well.
band_performance.Billy: Kreutzmann holds down a powerful backbeat that propels the Dark Star and the upbeat numbers.
